title: Sales by Customer counts each customer once and leaves out undone invoices
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
  2. In the top bar, click the location name at the top left (e.g. ShopHub) and choose your test location: one where nobody else invoices, issues credits or clocks time this week. The next step checks that it is quiet. If no location you can reach is quiet, create one once and reuse it on every later run: Settings > Locations > add a location (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dashboard Quiet") > save, give your user access, then choose it here. Locations cannot be deleted, so never create a second one.
  3. Check the location is quiet: click Dashboard in the top menu, click the range pill on the Revenue tile and choose This Week. Revenue must read $0.00 with 0 Invoices under it. If it shows anything else, choose another location.
  4. Run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  5. Create four test customers the standard way (Customers > New Customer, then a contact and an asset with that contact), e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST SBC 1" to "ZZAUTOTEST SBC 4".
  6. Invoice work orders with these standard steps for each one: Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer and its asset > Create. Set Service Advisor and mileage, add one line (e.g. Estimated Time 1.00 at $100.00 per hour, Tech Time 1.00, Approved), type a Story, set the line Complete, Complete Work Order, Mark Reviewed, Finance > Create Invoice, close the payment dialog without paying.
    • Customer 1: two invoiced work orders.
    • Customer 2: one invoiced work order.
    • Customer 3: one invoiced work order, then reverse it: Finance tab > the invoice's three dots > Reverse > confirm.
    • Customer 4: one invoiced work order left unpaid and unsent, then void it: on its Lines tab add a New Line (e.g. 0.50 hour) and save. Do not create a new invoice for it.
custom_steps:
1. Count by hand: Customer 1 (two invoices, counted once) + Customer 2 = 2 customers. Customer 3 (reversed) and Customer 4 (voided) add none.
  2. Click Dashboard in the top menu.
  3. On the Sales by Customer tile click the range pill (it opens on Last 12 Months) and choose This Week.
  4. Write down the headline.
  5. Click View details under the tile and write down the customers listed and their Invoices count.
  6. Click the arrow icon beside "Sales by Customer" on the tile (its tooltip names the report).
  7. On the Sales By Customer report set the Date control to This week and count the customer rows.
  8. Click Work Orders, open Customer 2's work order, Finance tab > the invoice's three dots > Reverse > confirm.
  9. Click Dashboard, set Sales by Customer to This Week again and write down the headline.
  10. Try to make an invoice with no customer: Parts > Part Sales > New Part Sale, and see whether it can be invoiced without choosing a customer. If the screen insists on a customer, stop this step.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The headline reads "2 customers": Customer 1 counts once although it has two invoices.
  • The detail table lists Customer 1 (Invoices 2) and Customer 2 (Invoices 1). Customer 3 and Customer 4 are not listed.
  • The Sales By Customer report for This week lists the same two customers, so its count matches the tile.
  • After reversing Customer 2's invoice the headline reads "1 customer" (singular).
  • If you could invoice sales with no customer, all of them together add exactly one customer to the count, however many such invoices there are. If you could not, write "no-customer invoice not reachable by hand" in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3), story SV-9577 (S5); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-R2 Sales by Customer row, S3-E2, S3-R1), S5 (S5-R1, S5-R2, S5-E3). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 08_Customers_After (table: Customer, Invoices, Labor Delta, Subtotal).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R2: “Each measure is calculated as defined in the table below.”
  • S3-R2 table row (Sales by Customer (count)): “| Sales by Customer (count) | The count of distinct customers with sales in the selected range. | Sales By Customer report |”
  • S5-R1: “The Sales by Customer tile headline is the count of distinct customers with sales in the selected range.”
  • S5-R2: “The Sales by Customer headline reads "{count} customer" when the count is one and "{count} customers" otherwise.”
  • S5-E3: “Sales made on an invoice with no company are counted together as a single "no company" customer in the Sales by Customer count.”
  • S3-E2: “A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.”
  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
